Subject: Customer Success Charter — Helix Health: mutual next steps & milestones

Hi Clara — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed mutual next-steps charter so we can lock on milestones and owners. Please flag anything I misunderstood.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- High token volumes on triage workflows causing unpredictable latency during peak windows (ER triage and prior auth).
- Strict data residency and audit requirements; SOC2 evidence and API audit logs are gating procurement.
- Goal: Reduce median inference latency by ~40% at 8k concurrent requests while keeping PII on-prem or in private VPC.

Proposed Mutual Next-Steps Charter (draft)
1) Pilot environment & scope — Redwood Dedicated (private VPC) for triage NLU (2 models)
   - Target start: 2026-10-04
   - Owner (Helix): Clara Voss (Clinical Ops)
   - Owner (Redwood): Jasmine Liu (AE) / Ben Carter (Solutions Eng)
2) Security & compliance checklist — SOC2 artifacts + logging spec review
   - Target review: 2026-09-28
   - Owner (Helix): security contact (please confirm)
   - Owner (Redwood): Lauren Bishop (CS) / Security team
3) Eval metrics & success criteria: 40% latency reduction at 8k concurrent; API throughput >= X rps, accuracy delta within 1.5% baseline
   - Decision checkpoint: Exec sign-off after pilot (target 2026-11-01)
4) Procurement & PO timeline
   - Legal + procurement review window: 2026-10-18 — 2026-11-05

Attachments: Helix_MPA_draft_v1.pdf (draft charter), SOC2-evidence-list.xlsx (sample list, not exhaustive). I attached the draft MPA for you and Ben to review.

Next asks
- Can you confirm the Helix stakeholders for Security and Procurement?
- Any redlines we should incorporate before Ben sketches the infra diagram?
- If these dates look broadly right, I can circulate v2 with concrete SLAs and an internal pre-pilot checklist.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite to align owners if that helps.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192
